# Duckpad 0.10.3
This patch improves editing latency in very long lines, including large minified JSON files.
- Faster ASCII cursor coordinates, line layout, wrapping and brace matching reduce work shared by all document types. - Long single-line JSON reuses verified unchanged syntax and folding results, including recovery after temporarily invalid input. - Native multi-character input avoids repeating full line layout for every character while preserving editing notifications and Undo/Redo.
App and helpers: **0.10.3 (55)**. Requires **macOS 13 or later**. Universal binaries support Apple Silicon and Intel. Existing documents, sessions, settings and the native plugin ABI remain compatible.
## Installation
Download `Duckpad-0.10.3-universal.dmg` and drag Duckpad into Applications, or extract `Duckpad-0.10.3-universal.zip`. Verify the downloads against `SHA256SUMS.txt`. The signed Sparkle update feed is published after the release archive is uploaded.
## Validation and limitations
The 9,184,692-byte single-line ASCII JSON reference fixture completed four separate Release benchmark runs, rotating the first editing position. All 3,072 measured operations stayed below 50 ms; the highest latency was 42.7 ms. Measurements include native text-input queries, status calculation, synchronous drawing and layer flush. They cover insertion, deletion, bursts, selection replacement, 256-character input and byte-exact Undo/Redo. This is a fixture-specific measurement on the development Apple Silicon Mac, not a guarantee for every document or machine.
192 focused editor tests passed. Another 204 differential checks matched the unmodified engine for syntax/folding, layout and brace matching. Full-suite compilation is blocked by an existing Swift concurrency error in `MenuPresentationSpy.swift`; the targeted editor suites compile and pass.
JSON caching applies to complete single physical lines between 64 KiB and 32 MiB and uses additional memory proportional to document size. Other syntax lexers and very long Unicode or tab-containing lines can still exceed 50 ms. Shared engine improvements do not replace their full-line syntax analysis or Unicode shaping. These remaining cases are tracked in the [long-line performance audit](https://github.com/namJeongwan/duckpad/blob/v0.10.3/docs/wiki/long-line-performance-audit.md).
The default build is ad-hoc signed, without Developer ID signing or Apple notarization. Physical Intel hardware, macOS 13 and live Korean IME were not tested for this patch. Interactive system picker smoke checks are skipped unless explicitly enabled.
